stem: Which anti-seizure medication class should be avoided in juvenile myoclonic epilepsy because it may worsen seizures?

options.text: Sodium channel blockers such as carbamazepine

explanation: Sodium channel blockers such as carbamazepine should be avoided in juvenile myoclonic epilepsy because they can exacerbate seizures.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because sodium channel blockers such as carbamazepine can worsen myoclonic and generalised seizures in juvenile myoclonic epilepsy.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because levetiracetam is a commonly used treatment for juvenile myoclonic epilepsy.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because sodium valproate is highly effective for juvenile myoclonic epilepsy, although its use requires caution in some patients.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because lamotrigine can be used in juvenile myoclonic epilepsy, even though it may be less effective for myoclonus in some patients.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because clonazepam may help suppress myoclonic seizures rather than exacerbate them.

source.hint: Focus on a specific class of anti-seizure medications that interact poorly with generalized idiopathic epilepsies.
